False positive: flags the .ghost-glyph decorative watermark ('Aa' at 580px, color rgba(245,243,238,0.045), z-index:0, pointer-events:none), a near-invisible background texture sitting behind the real content layer (.content-col at z-index:1), not legible body text. The static analyzer resolves the composited near-transparent color against the ink background as if it were foreground text needing AA contrast; visually confirmed via rendered screenshot that the glyph reads as a whisper-quiet texture, not text to be read.

Text #f5f3ee on accent #3a64ff (4.3:1, just under 4.5:1 AA) is the app's own established primary-button/selected-chip treatment, depicted here inside literal screenshots of real in-app UI ('No app de verdade' — Continuar CTA, Intermediário selected chip). Changing it here would misrepresent the actual app's design system rather than fix a slide-specific decoration choice; advisory severity, pre-existing brand color pairing used identically throughout the app, not introduced by this pass.
